subject: scaly-foot snail
title: This Snail Builds Its Shell Out of Iron, Two Miles Under the Sea

scenes.text: One snail on Earth wears armour made of iron.
The scaly-foot snail lives nearly two miles down in the Indian Ocean, beside scalding volcanic vents.
Its shell has three layers, and the outer one is iron sulfide. Its foot is covered in iron-plated scales.
No other known animal builds iron into its skeleton.
The US Army studied it to design better armour.
But miners want the metal around those vents. In 2019 it became the first species listed as endangered by deep-sea mining.

description:
The scaly-foot snail, Chrysomallon squamiferum, is the only animal known to build iron sulfide into its shell and the scales on its foot.
It lives at a handful of hydrothermal vents in the Indian Ocean, as deep as 2,900 meters. Its shell has three layers: a calcified inner layer, an organic middle layer and an outer layer fortified with iron sulfides, and the US Army has studied it for armour design. In July 2019 the IUCN listed it as Endangered, the first species given that status because of the threat of deep-sea mining; two of the three sites it was known from were already cleared for mining.
Should the seabed be mined? Comment below.
first_comment: It gets most of its food from bacteria living inside its own body. Iron shell or built-in food supply: which would you take?
